subject: maths
title: Shapes, Direction and Movement - Patterns and Directions
introductionText:
Term 2 · Geometry
Shapes, Direction and Movement —
Patterns and Directions
The Big Idea: A pattern repeats, so we can say what comes next. Directions tell us how to
move: forwards, backwards, turn left, turn right.
Say It Like This
Read aloud
"Look: red, blue, red, blue... what comes next? Red! The bit that repeats is red, blue. Now
stand up. Take 2 steps forwards — the way your nose points. Take 1 step backwards.
Now turn to face the window. You moved, but your feet stayed on the same spot —
turning changes the way you face."
Watch Out For
The slip almost every child makes
Continuing a pattern by copying the last shape. After red, blue, red, blue he adds
another blue. Ask him to say the pattern aloud in a rhythm — "red-blue, red-blue" — the
next word is obvious when it's sung.
Left and right. These take years to settle. Put a sticker on his right hand for the games.
Remember: when he faces you, his right hand is on your left.
Try It at Home
Game 1 — Pasta necklace (10 minutes)
Use two kinds of pasta. Make a pattern: tube, shell, tube, shell. He continues it on a piece
of string. Then try a harder one: tube, tube, shell. Ask him to invent a pattern for you to
continue — and make a mistake on purpose so he can catch it.
Game 2 — The robot (10 minutes)
He is a robot and only obeys exact orders. Hide a treat. Guide him with commands: "3
steps forwards. Turn right. 2 steps forwards." Then swap: he gives the orders and you are
the robot. Obey exactly what he says, even when it's wrong — it's the fastest way for him
to learn.
A repeating pattern — what comes next?
?
The robot's moves:
1. 3 steps forwards
2. turn right
3. 3 steps forwards
→ it reaches the star!
Ask what shape comes next. Then trace the robot's path with his finger, saying each move aloud.
More examples to talk about
• Patterns are everywhere: stripes on a shirt, tiles on the kitchen floor, the days of the
week.
• A pattern can repeat colours, shapes, sizes or sounds: clap, clap, stamp.
• A square and a rectangle are the same in some ways (4 sides, 4 corners) and different in
one way (a square's sides are all equal).
• A 2D shape is flat; a 3D shape is solid. You can draw a cube's face, but not hold a
drawing.
• Tricky: walking backwards means you move the way your back faces, but you keep
facing the same way.
Key Words
pattern repeat sequence next forwards backwards turn left right

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Continue the pattern: red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue, ,
Make your own pattern with 2 shapes. Draw it.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Any pattern where a part clearly repeats at least twice.

sourceQuestions.sourceText:
You stand facing the door. You take 3 steps forwards and 1 step backwards. How many
steps are you from where you started?
True or false? A cube is a flat (2D) shape.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: False. A cube is solid — it is 3D.

sourceQuestions.sourceText:
Say one thing that is the same and one thing that is different about a square and a
rectangle.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText:
Same: 4 sides and 4 corners. Different: a square's sides are all equal; a rectangle has two
long and two short sides.

How many sides does a square have?

Moving the way your back faces is moving...
( backwards ) ( sideways ) ( forwards )

Turning means...
( walking a long way ) ( jumping up ) ( changing the way you face )

A 3D shape is...
( only a drawing ) ( solid — you can hold it ) ( flat )
